"""Spot-check read: runs 6 (electron n=+3.2e12) and 7 (hole n=-1.2e12). Onset + FFT vs F_L."""
import numpy as np, matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from hera.analysis import open_run, sdh_onset, sdh_fft, luttinger_frequency, SdhOnsetError

CAL = dict(c_tg=2.796e-03, c_bg=2.161e-03, n_offset=-0.0894, D_offset=-0.013)
SPEC = {6: ("electron", +3.2), 7: ("hole", -1.2)}
I_FS = 50e-6 / 1.0  # sr1 sensitivity 50 uV, gain 1

fig, axes = plt.subplots(3, 2, figsize=(13, 11))
for k, rid in enumerate((6, 7)):
    r = open_run(f"data/{rid}")
    side, n12 = SPEC[rid]
    B = r.col("magnet_field")
    I = r.col("sr0_X") / (-1e6)
    V = r.col("sr1_X") / 1.0
    R = V / I
    t = r.col("time"); T = r.col("T_sample")
    o = np.argsort(B); B, R, Rs = B[o], R[o], None
    Rs = R
    F_L = luttinger_frequency(abs(n12) * 1e12 * 1e4)  # cm^-2 -> m^-2
    I_bias = float(r.meta["measurement_config"].get("drive_V", 1.0)) / 1e8 if "drive_V" in r.meta.get("measurement_config", {}) else 1.0 / 1e8
    print("=" * 70)
    print(f"run {rid} ({side}, n = {n12:+.2f}e12): {len(B)} pts, B {B.min():.2f}-{B.max():.2f} T, "
          f"wall {(t.max()-t.min())/60:.1f} min -> {(t.max()-t.min())/len(B):.2f} s/pt")
    print(f"  T_sample {T.min():.3f}-{T.max():.3f} K; R {R.min():.0f}-{R.max():.0f} Ohm; I_meas {np.median(np.abs(I))*1e9:.3f} nA")
    print(f"  F_L(g=4) = {F_L:.2f} T; full-scale R = {I_FS/np.median(np.abs(I)):.0f} Ohm; max |V|/FS = {np.abs(V).max()/50e-6*100:.1f}%")
    # leakage
    print(f"  |I_tg| max {np.abs(r.col('k_2400_tg_curr')).max()*1e12:.0f} pA, |I_bg| max {np.abs(r.col('k_2400_bg_curr')).max()*1e12:.0f} pA")

    ax = axes[0, k]
    ax.plot(B, R, lw=0.7)
    ax.set_xlabel("B (T)"); ax.set_ylabel("Rxx (Ohm)"); ax.set_title(f"run {rid} raw — {side}, n={n12:+.2f}e12")

    # onset
    try:
        on = sdh_onset(R, B, r_full_scale=I_FS / np.median(np.abs(I)))
        print("  --- sdh_onset ---")
        print("   " + on.summary().replace("\n", "\n   "))
    except SdhOnsetError as e:
        on = None
        print(f"  --- sdh_onset FAILED: {e}")

    # background-subtracted trace over the usable window
    b_lo = on.onset_b if on is not None else 1.0
    b_hi = (on.clip_high_b or B.max()) if on is not None else B.max()
    m = (B >= max(b_lo, 0.3)) & (B <= b_hi)
    cf = np.polyfit(B[m], R[m], 5)
    dR = R[m] - np.polyval(cf, B[m])
    ax = axes[1, k]
    ax.plot(1 / B[m], dR, lw=0.8)
    ax.set_xlabel("1/B (1/T)"); ax.set_ylabel("dRxx (Ohm)")
    ax.set_title(f"bg-subtracted (deg5), B {max(b_lo,0.3):.2f}-{b_hi:.2f} T")

    # FFT, a few cutoffs
    ax = axes[2, k]
    for cut in (max(b_lo, 0.5), 1.0, 2.0, 3.0):
        if cut >= b_hi - 0.5:
            continue
        f, sp = sdh_fft(R[:, None], B, b_range=(cut, b_hi), bg_degree=5, log=False, nfft=2048)
        s = sp[0]
        ax.plot(f, s / s[f > 1].max(), lw=0.9, label=f"cut {cut:.2f} T")
        pk = [(f[i], s[i]) for i in range(2, len(f) - 2)
              if s[i] > s[i - 1] and s[i] > s[i + 1] and s[i] > 0.08 * s[f > 1].max() and f[i] > 1]
        pk.sort(key=lambda x: -x[1])
        print(f"  FFT [{cut:.2f}-{b_hi:.2f} T] dF={1/(1/max(cut,1e-9)-1/b_hi):.2f} T  peaks: " +
              ", ".join(f"{p[0]:.1f}T({p[1]/pk[0][1]:.2f})" for p in pk[:6]))
    ax.axvline(F_L, color="r", ls="--", lw=1, label=f"F_L {F_L:.1f} T")
    ax.axvline(0.72 * F_L, color="g", ls=":", lw=1, label="0.72/0.28 F_L")
    ax.axvline(0.28 * F_L, color="g", ls=":", lw=1)
    ax.set_xlim(0, min(2.2 * F_L, f.max())); ax.set_xlabel("F (T)"); ax.set_ylabel("|FFT| (norm)")
    ax.legend(fontsize=7); ax.set_title(f"1/B FFT — run {rid}")

fig.tight_layout()
fig.savefig("hera_scratch/spot_runs67.png", dpi=110)
print("saved hera_scratch/spot_runs67.png")

"""Spot-check read: runs 6 (electron n=+3.2e12) and 7 (hole n=-1.2e12). Onset + FFT vs F_L."""
import numpy as np, matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from hera.analysis import open_run, sdh_onset, sdh_fft, luttinger_frequency, SdhOnsetError

CAL = dict(c_tg=2.796e-03, c_bg=2.161e-03, n_offset=-0.0894, D_offset=-0.013)
SPEC = {6: ("electron", +3.2), 7: ("hole", -1.2)}
I_FS = 50e-6 / 1.0  # sr1 sensitivity 50 uV, gain 1

fig, axes = plt.subplots(3, 2, figsize=(13, 11))
for k, rid in enumerate((6, 7)):
    r = open_run(f"data/{rid}")
    side, n12 = SPEC[rid]
    B = r.col("magnet_field")
    I = r.col("sr0_X") / (-1e6)
    V = r.col("sr1_X") / 1.0
    R = V / I
    t = r.col("time"); T = r.col("T_sample")
    o = np.argsort(B); B, R, Rs = B[o], R[o], None
    Rs = R
    F_L = luttinger_frequency(abs(n12) * 1e12 * 1e4)  # cm^-2 -> m^-2
    I_bias = float(r.meta["measurement_config"].get("drive_V", 1.0)) / 1e8 if "drive_V" in r.meta.get("measurement_config", {}) else 1.0 / 1e8
    print("=" * 70)
    print(f"run {rid} ({side}, n = {n12:+.2f}e12): {len(B)} pts, B {B.min():.2f}-{B.max():.2f} T, "
          f"wall {(t.max()-t.min())/60:.1f} min -> {(t.max()-t.min())/len(B):.2f} s/pt")
    print(f"  T_sample {T.min():.3f}-{T.max():.3f} K; R {R.min():.0f}-{R.max():.0f} Ohm; I_meas {np.median(np.abs(I))*1e9:.3f} nA")
    print(f"  F_L(g=4) = {F_L:.2f} T; full-scale R = {I_FS/np.median(np.abs(I)):.0f} Ohm; max |V|/FS = {np.abs(V).max()/50e-6*100:.1f}%")
    # leakage
    print(f"  |I_tg| max {np.abs(r.col('k_2400_tg_curr')).max()*1e12:.0f} pA, |I_bg| max {np.abs(r.col('k_2400_bg_curr')).max()*1e12:.0f} pA")

    ax = axes[0, k]
    ax.plot(B, R, lw=0.7)
    ax.set_xlabel("B (T)"); ax.set_ylabel("Rxx (Ohm)"); ax.set_title(f"run {rid} raw — {side}, n={n12:+.2f}e12")

    # onset
    try:
        on = sdh_onset(R, B, r_full_scale=I_FS / np.median(np.abs(I)))
        print("  --- sdh_onset ---")
        print("   " + on.summary().replace("\n", "\n   "))
    except SdhOnsetError as e:
        on = None
        print(f"  --- sdh_onset FAILED: {e}")

    # background-subtracted trace over the usable window
    b_lo = on.onset_b if on is not None else 1.0
    b_hi = (on.clip_high_b or B.max()) if on is not None else B.max()
    m = (B >= max(b_lo, 0.3)) & (B <= b_hi)
    cf = np.polyfit(B[m], R[m], 5)
    dR = R[m] - np.polyval(cf, B[m])
    ax = axes[1, k]
    ax.plot(1 / B[m], dR, lw=0.8)
    ax.set_xlabel("1/B (1/T)"); ax.set_ylabel("dRxx (Ohm)")
    ax.set_title(f"bg-subtracted (deg5), B {max(b_lo,0.3):.2f}-{b_hi:.2f} T")

    # FFT, a few cutoffs
    ax = axes[2, k]
    for cut in (max(b_lo, 0.5), 1.0, 2.0, 3.0):
        if cut >= b_hi - 0.5:
            continue
        f, sp = sdh_fft(R[:, None], B, b_range=(cut, b_hi), bg_degree=5, log=False, nfft=2048)
        s = sp[0]
        ax.plot(f, s / s[f > 1].max(), lw=0.9, label=f"cut {cut:.2f} T")
        pk = [(f[i], s[i]) for i in range(2, len(f) - 2)
              if s[i] > s[i - 1] and s[i] > s[i + 1] and s[i] > 0.08 * s[f > 1].max() and f[i] > 1]
        pk.sort(key=lambda x: -x[1])
        print(f"  FFT [{cut:.2f}-{b_hi:.2f} T] dF={1/(1/max(cut,1e-9)-1/b_hi):.2f} T  peaks: " +
              ", ".join(f"{p[0]:.1f}T({p[1]/pk[0][1]:.2f})" for p in pk[:6]))
    ax.axvline(F_L, color="r", ls="--", lw=1, label=f"F_L {F_L:.1f} T")
    ax.axvline(0.72 * F_L, color="g", ls=":", lw=1, label="0.72/0.28 F_L")
    ax.axvline(0.28 * F_L, color="g", ls=":", lw=1)
    ax.set_xlim(0, min(2.2 * F_L, f.max())); ax.set_xlabel("F (T)"); ax.set_ylabel("|FFT| (norm)")
    ax.legend(fontsize=7); ax.set_title(f"1/B FFT — run {rid}")

fig.tight_layout()
fig.savefig("hera_scratch/spot_runs67.png", dpi=110)

# Tetralayer FS-count forward model — ABAB vs ABCA (vs ABCB)

Backs the `recipes/investigations/tetralayer-stacking-fs-count.md` investigation.
This model computes the **B = 0 Fermi-surface count**, the **Onsager
frequencies F(n)** (and vs interlayer potential u_D for ABCA), and the
**cyclotron masses m\*(n)** the FS-count read overlays on data — ABAB a pair
partitioning F_L (≈ 0.72 / 0.28 with φ²-split masses in the decomposition
limit; the key table below carries the real F(n)) vs ABCA's single
post-cascade pocket at F_L, with ABCB a qualitative cubic + Dirac pair.
**Both carrier signs**: the sign of the input density selects electron
(n > 0) or hole (n < 0) doping.

The survey that grounds it (band structure, the four ingested papers, the
feasibility framing) is `docs/tetralayer-stacking-extraction-survey.md`; read
it for the physics. This README covers what the tools are and how to run them.

## Files

| File | What it does |
|---|---|
| `synth_fan.py` | Synthetic Rxx(n, B) fan generator on the model's F(n)/m\*(n): LK thermal + Dingle dressing, 2nd harmonics, background, noise; optional lever-arm scale error, breakdown sum-tone, mixed-domain superposition. Ground truth per column in `truth.json`. |
| `synth_eval.py` | Mechanical recipe evaluator over the synthetic fans (pipeline FFT → Luttinger-aware harmonic screen → global scale pin → template match → B-window split → adjacent-N). Six-case suite + `RESULTS.md` in `$HERA_DATA/tetralayer-synth-validation/`. |
| `JULIA_CROSSCHECK.md` | Independent-implementation eigenvalue comparison (machine precision; see Validation). |
| `fs_count_b0.py` | B = 0 FS count + Onsager F(n) + m\*(n), both carrier signs. **ABAB** from the 2N-band SWMcC Hamiltonian (Koshino–McCann PRB 83, 165443 Eq. 1, N = 4), graphite parameters, via a rotationally-symmetric signed-density radial solve (electron pockets +k²/π, hole pockets −k²/π; the two bilayer-like blocks emerge automatically). **ABCA** from the 8-band continuum model of arXiv 2606.05356 S15 (Eqs. 8–14), parameter Set 1, on a 2D k-grid (trigonal warping → the low-density three-pocket → annulus → single Lifshitz cascade); interlayer potential u_D via the onsite U_l structure. **ABCB** qualitative, via the generic linkage builder. A generic `build_h(kx, ky, seq, p, ud)` dispatches any stacking string ('ABAB','ABCA','ABA','ABC',…) to a Bernal / rhombohedral / mixed block builder by link sense, so trilayer sequences run for backtests. Counts distinct extremal-orbit frequencies F = (ℏ/2πe)·A_k, positive/area-based for electron- and hole-like orbits alike. Pure numpy/scipy; `selftest()`/`__main__` runs every validation gate and prints the key tables. |

## API (call shapes)

- `abab_fs(n, ud=0.0) -> (E_F, [(F, kF), ...])` — every ABAB Onsager orbit at
  E_F, sorted by F.
- `abab_mstar(n, ud=0.0) -> [(F, m*/m_e), ...]` — per-orbit cyclotron masses,
  m\* = ℏ²k_F/|dE/dk|, same orbits/order as `abab_fs`.
- `abca_fs(n, ud=0.0) -> (E_F, topo, n_components, n_freq, F_total)` — topology
  from connected components of the Fermi sea (single / annulus / k-pocket).
- `abca_mstar(n, ud=0.0) -> (F_total, m*/m_e)` — from dn/dE_F on the same solve;
  pocket-summed in the cascade region.
- `abcb_fs(n, ud=0.0) -> (E_F, [(F, ncomp), ...])` — **qualitative**, electron
  side only: the two low-energy conduction tones (cubic J = 3 + Dirac J = 1).
- Generic underneath: `bernal_fs`/`bernal_mstar`/`rhombo_fs`/`rhombo_mstar`
  take a sequence + `Params`; `build_h(kx, ky, seq, p, ud)` returns the
  Hamiltonian; `ABAB`, `ABCA`, `ABA_TRI` are the parameter sets.

Masses are positive for electron- and hole-like orbits alike; the carrier sign
comes from the input n.

## Domain — loud, never clamped

The solvers raise `ValueError` (naming the covered range) for any density
outside the solved table; E_F rows whose Fermi contour would cross the k-grid
edge are excluded from the table on both sides. Solved coverage at u_D = 0:
ABAB ≈ −17.7…+17.1 ×10¹² cm⁻², ABCA ≈ ±11.5 ×10¹² cm⁻² — comfortably beyond
the ±8×10¹² cm⁻² design target.

## Parameters and validity

**Semi-quantitative — trust topology, shape, and partition, not absolute
frequencies.** The discriminating outputs are the FS count, the ABAB partition
and its φ²-split masses, and the model-independent Luttinger sum
Σ±f = (h/4e)|n|. Absolute frequencies inherit the hopping-parameter error bars.

- **ABAB**: Koshino–McCann graphite SWMcC set {γ₀ = 3.0, γ₁ = 0.4, γ₂ = −0.02,
  γ₄ = 0.04, γ₅ = 0.04, Δ′ = 0.05 eV}, all remote couplings ON. **γ₃ = 0**:
  the BL-contour trigonal warping is neglected so the solve stays radial (same
  precedent and caveat as the trilayer ABA treatment — γ₃ touches only the
  low-|n| BL fine structure). The 0.724 / 0.276 partition and φ² ≈ 2.618 mass
  ratio are the **low-n parabolic (decomposition) asymptote**; two effects
  distort them away from it — non-parabolicity (the bilayer bands bend toward
  linear) pulls the ratio *down* with rising |n|, while the γ₂-scale
  band-bottom offset dominates at low |n| and washes out with rising |n|. In
  the full model the electron-side partition passes through ≈ 0.73 near
  |n| ≈ 6×10¹²; the hole side runs lower (≈ 0.64) from the Δ′/γ₄ e–h asymmetry
  and the near-CNP semimetal overlap (§ below). Even-N has no mirror plane, so
  the two bilayer blocks are mixed by γ₂/γ₅ at the ~20 meV scale and inter-block
  magnetic breakdown is symmetry-allowed — the two-FS picture is exact only
  above that scale.
- **ABCA**: arXiv 2606.05356 S15 Set 1 {γ₀ = 3.1, γ₁ = 0.38, γ₂ = −0.015,
  γ₃ = 0.29, γ₄ = 0.141, δ = 0.0105, Δ₂ = 0.002 eV}, **γ₃ ON** (trigonal
  warping is the physics of the low-density cascade, not fine structure).
  u_D enters as a linear interlayer potential V_l = l·u_D (no Hartree screening).

**cyclotron masses m\*(n)** the FS-count read overlays on data — ABAB a pair
partitioning F_L (≈ 0.72 / 0.28 with φ²-split masses in the decomposition
limit; the key table below carries the real F(n)) vs ABCA's single
post-cascade pocket at F_L, with ABCB a qualitative cubic + Dirac pair.
**Both carrier signs**: the sign of the input density selects electron
(n > 0) or hole (n < 0) doping.

The survey that grounds it (band structure, the four ingested papers, the
feasibility framing) is `docs/tetralayer-stacking-extraction-survey.md`; read
it for the physics. This README covers what the tools are and how to run them.

## Files

| File | What it does |
|---|---|
| `synth_fan.py` | Synthetic Rxx(n, B) fan generator on the model's F(n)/m\*(n): LK thermal + Dingle dressing, 2nd harmonics, background, noise; optional lever-arm scale error, breakdown sum-tone, mixed-domain superposition. Ground truth per column in `truth.json`. |
| `synth_eval.py` | Mechanical recipe evaluator over the synthetic fans (pipeline FFT → Luttinger-aware harmonic screen → global scale pin → template match → B-window split → adjacent-N). Six-case suite + `RESULTS.md` in `$HERA_DATA/tetralayer-synth-validation/`. |
| `JULIA_CROSSCHECK.md` | Independent-implementation eigenvalue comparison (machine precision; see Validation). |
| `fs_count_b0.py` | B = 0 FS count + Onsager F(n) + m\*(n), both carrier signs. **ABAB** from the 2N-band SWMcC Hamiltonian (Koshino–McCann PRB 83, 165443 Eq. 1, N = 4), graphite parameters, via a rotationally-symmetric signed-density radial solve (electron pockets +k²/π, hole pockets −k²/π; the two bilayer-like blocks emerge automatically). **ABCA** from the 8-band continuum model of arXiv 2606.05356 S15 (Eqs. 8–14), parameter Set 1, on a 2D k-grid (trigonal warping → the low-density three-pocket → annulus → single Lifshitz cascade); interlayer potential u_D via the onsite U_l structure. **ABCB** qualitative, via the generic linkage builder. A generic `build_h(kx, ky, seq, p, ud)` dispatches any stacking string ('ABAB','ABCA','ABA','ABC',…) to a Bernal / rhombohedral / mixed block builder by link sense, so trilayer sequences run for backtests. Counts distinct extremal-orbit frequencies F = (ℏ/2πe)·A_k, positive/area-based for electron- and hole-like orbits alike. Pure numpy/scipy; `selftest()`/`__main__` runs every validation gate and prints the key tables. |

## API (call shapes)

- `abab_fs(n, ud=0.0) -> (E_F, [(F, kF), ...])` — every ABAB Onsager orbit at
  E_F, sorted by F.
- `abab_mstar(n, ud=0.0) -> [(F, m*/m_e), ...]` — per-orbit cyclotron masses,
  m\* = ℏ²k_F/|dE/dk|, same orbits/order as `abab_fs`.
- `abca_fs(n, ud=0.0) -> (E_F, topo, n_components, n_freq, F_total)` — topology
  from connected components of the Fermi sea (single / annulus / k-pocket).
- `abca_mstar(n, ud=0.0) -> (F_total, m*/m_e)` — from dn/dE_F on the same solve;
  pocket-summed in the cascade region.
- `abcb_fs(n, ud=0.0) -> (E_F, [(F, ncomp), ...])` — **qualitative**, electron
  side only: the two low-energy conduction tones (cubic J = 3 + Dirac J = 1).
- Generic underneath: `bernal_fs`/`bernal_mstar`/`rhombo_fs`/`rhombo_mstar`
  take a sequence + `Params`; `build_h(kx, ky, seq, p, ud)` returns the
  Hamiltonian; `ABAB`, `ABCA`, `ABA_TRI` are the parameter sets.

Masses are positive for electron- and hole-like orbits alike; the carrier sign
comes from the input n.

## Domain — loud, never clamped

The solvers raise `ValueError` (naming the covered range) for any density
outside the solved table; E_F rows whose Fermi contour would cross the k-grid
edge are excluded from the table on both sides. Solved coverage at u_D = 0:
ABAB ≈ −17.7…+17.1 ×10¹² cm⁻², ABCA ≈ ±11.5 ×10¹² cm⁻² — comfortably beyond
the ±8×10¹² cm⁻² design target.

## Parameters and validity

**Semi-quantitative — trust topology, shape, and partition, not absolute

Luttinger-solid ((h/4e)|n| by area conservation), insensitive to the
  parameter error bars.
- **ABCB**: qualitative only, via the mixed-linkage builder run on the ABCA
  hopping magnitudes. Reproduces the J = 3 cubic main band + J = 1 Dirac-like
  partner rising from the ~δ (≈ 10 meV) gap; the two tones Luttinger-sum to
  F_L. **Absolute frequencies and the partition are not calibrated** — trust
  the two-tone topology and order of magnitude only. Not gated.
- ABAB is semimetallic near the CNP: for small |n| tiny electron and hole
  pockets coexist (the two blocks' band bottoms are offset at the γ₂ scale),
  the orbit list reports all of them, and only the **signed** sum of
  frequencies equals (h/4e)|n| there.

## Validation

All six gates pass (`selftest()`); residuals quoted are the actual run.

- **Gate 1 — ABAB decomposition limit**: with γ₂ = γ₅ = Δ′ = γ₄ = γ₃ = 0 the
  k = 0 spectrum is {±0.618γ₁, ±1.618γ₁, 0×4} (λ = 2cos2π/5, 2cos π/5) to
  1.7×10⁻¹² eV; the high-density Onsager partition → 0.7236 / 0.2764 and mass
  ratio → 2.618 in the low-n parabolic limit (0.722 / 2.574 at |n| = 0.25×10¹²,
  monotonically degrading with non-parabolicity: 0.692 / 2.01 at 6×10¹²).
- **Gate 2 — Luttinger sum** Σ±f = (h/4e)|n| reproduces on **both carrier
  signs** for ABAB (signed) and ABCA (single pocket) at every density tested
  (worst residual 0.015 T, grid discretization).
- **Gate 3a — ABCA higher-order vHS**: the analytic E₂ (S15 Eq. 17) crosses
  zero at the critical u_D solving Eq. 18, u_D = 42.82 meV; the numerical
  lowest-conduction-band k → 0 curvature flips sign at 43 meV, tracking E₂ to
  ≤ 0.3% across u_D ∈ [30, 55] meV.
- **Gate 3b — ABCA Lifshitz cascade**: at u_D = 43 meV the Fermi sea passes
  **three-pocket → annulus → single** as n grows (topology sequence matches
  Fig S29-c). Boundaries land at n ≈ 1.5 / 2.6 ×10¹² — ~2–4× above the S29-c
  digitization; **qualitative agreement only** (topology + order of magnitude),
  as scoped by the survey.
- **Gate 4 — trilayer backtest**: the generic builder run as 'ABA' with the
  frozen `models/trilayer_fs_count` parameters reproduces that model's
  `aba_fs` F(n) at n = ±{1,2,3,6}×10¹² to **≤ 0.17%** (e.g. +6×10¹²:
  [7.01, 55.03] vs [7.02, 55.02] T; −3×10¹²: [4.35, 26.66] vs [4.35, 26.67] T).
  The generic 'ABC' single-pocket F(n) matches (h/4e)|n| to 0.01% (Luttinger —
  the frozen ABC is a MacDonald two-band projection, so only its
  Luttinger-pinned F is comparable).
- **Gate 5 — m\* identities**: ABAB per-orbit masses satisfy the thermodynamic
  DOS identity dn/dE = (2/πℏ²)·Σ±m\* against the density table (worst 0.2%);
  ABCA m\* matches an independent finite-difference of E_F(n) (worst 1.7%).
- **Synthetic-fan recovery** (`synth_fan.py` + `synth_eval.py`; artifacts in
  `$HERA_DATA/tetralayer-synth-validation/RESULTS.md`): six dressed synthetic
  fans (clean ABAB hole/electron incl. the low-n trap, clean ABCA, breakdown
  sum-tone adversarial, 12% lever-arm scale error, trilayer-mislabeled-4L) all
  classified correctly by the mechanical recipe logic; global scale pinned to
  ≤ 2% (the 1.12 case recovered exactly); claimed-tone frequency error < 0.5%
  median; every trap navigated (low-n ambiguity flagged not called; breakdown
  identified by B-window split; adjacent-N fired on the mislabeled case).
  Method findings folded into the recipe: Luttinger-aware harmonic screen,
  cross-column adjacent-N consensus, narrow-window breakdown resolvability.
- **Agent-in-harness replay (rung 3b + adjacent-N amendment)** — three
  classification-frontier fixtures
  (`hera/test-cases/{2026-05-14-QC0512,2026-05-21-QC0531,2026-02-17-RPL19}-stacking-fan`)
  through `hera-replay`, n = 3 each, production HERA tier: the F_L-tone-origin
  discrimination fires 3/3 (breakdown fixture — ABAB strong, no eager ABCA);
  operating-point discipline holds 3/3 (real D = 1 fan declined); the
  adjacent-N guard fires 3/3 name-blind on the trilayer-carded-4LGr fixture
  under the recipe's binding dual-overlay gate, with no over-correction
  (genuine-ABAB replay 1/1; mechanical suite 6/6). Not elicited: the
  degeneracy audit (agents disqualify off-operating-point fans on D first).
  Scoring + prereg: `$HERA_DATA/tetralayer-replay-3b/`.
- **Julia cross-check** (`JULIA_CROSSCHECK.md`): `h_rhombo` agrees with the
  independent `RhombohedralGrapheneLandau.jl` implementation at the
  eigenvalue level to **machine precision** (linearized γ₀, matched Set-1
  parameters, valley K, |k| ≤ 0.5 nm⁻¹, u_D ∈ {0, 43 meV}); full-f(k) mode
  differs ≤ 6 meV at the window edge, the expected Dirac-linearization
  curvature (zero at K, ~|k|²). A γ₃-sign flip blows the comparison to
  > 50 meV — the trigonal-warping term the internal gates can't check is
  confirmed. Sign-convention note: julia stores signed γ₃ = −0.29 with
  t₃ = −γ₃; this model stores the magnitude with the sign in the builder —
  same matrix element.

### Real-data validation (RPL_19 / arXiv:2606.05356)

Validated against real Landau fans from RPL_19 (the paper's rmg19 device;
identity from matching gate-calibration constants + sweep-ids). Scripts
`rpl19_load.py` / `real_eval.py` / `lf_crosscheck.py` reuse the pipeline above;

  and flavor-polarized (a degeneracy read, not a stacking read); at the D=0.2,

    ax.plot(f[m], s[m] / s[m].max(), lw=1.0, label=f"bg_degree {deg}")

ax = axes[1, 0]

    f, sp = sdh_fft(R[:, None], B, b_range=(lo, hi), bg_degree=5, log=False, nfft=8192)
    s = sp[0]; m = (f > 2) & (f < 60)
    ax.plot(f[m], s[m] / s[m].max(), lw=1.0, label=f"{lab} (dF {1/(1/lo-1/hi):.2f})")
ax.axvline(F_L, color="r", ls="--"); ax.axvline(25.9, color="b", ls="--"); ax.axvline(7.2, color="g", ls="--")
for k in (2, 3, 4): ax.axvline(k * 7.3, color="k", ls=":", lw=0.7)
ax.set_xlabel("F (T)"); ax.legend(fontsize=7); ax.set_title("B-window split (F_L-tone origin probe)")

# peak table at the best window
print("\npeak tables:")
for (lo, hi) in windows:
    f, sp = sdh_fft(R[:, None], B, b_range=(lo, hi), bg_degree=5, log=False, nfft=8192)
    s = sp[0]
    m = (f > 2.5) & (f < 60)
    ff, ss = f[m], s[m]
    idx = [i for i in range(1, len(ss) - 1) if ss[i] > ss[i - 1] and ss[i] >= ss[i + 1]]
    idx.sort(key=lambda i: -ss[i])
    top = [(ff[i], ss[i] / ss[idx[0]]) for i in idx[:8]]
    print(f"  [{lo:4.1f}-{hi:4.1f}] dF={1/(1/lo-1/hi):5.2f}: " +
          ", ".join(f"{a:.1f}T({b:.2f})" for a, b in top))

ax.plot(1 / B[m], R[m] - np.polyval(cf, B[m]), lw=0.8)
ax.set_xlabel("1/B (1/T)"); ax.set_ylabel("dRxx (Ohm)"); ax.set_title("run 6 bg-subtracted, 1-10 T")
fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig("hera_scratch/spot_run6_hires.png", dpi=110)
print("saved hera_scratch/spot_run6_hires.png")

| `multisweep` | `(params, setpointslist, delay=0.0)` | `[time, *setpoints, *followed]` |
| `megasweep` | `(slow_param, slow_v, fast_param, fast_v, slow_delay=0.0, fast_delay=0.0, init_delay=True)` | `[time, slow, fast, *followed]` |
| `multimegasweep` | `(slow_params, slow_v_list, fast_params, fast_v_list, slow_delay=0.0, fast_delay=0.0, init_delay=True)` | `[time, *slow, *fast, *followed]` |

- **`sweep`** — 1D. Sets `param` to each setpoint, waits `delay`, measures.
- **`multisweep`** — 1D, several parameters **co-swept**. `params` and
  `setpointslist` are parallel lists; `setpointslist[i]` is the vector for
  `params[i]`, and **all vectors must be equal length** (raises otherwise). At
  point j every `params[i]` is set to `setpointslist[i][j]` — one path through
  N-space, not a grid (e.g. a fixed-D (Vtg, Vbg) line).
- **`megasweep`** — 2D grid: outer `slow_param` over `slow_v`, inner
  `fast_param` over `fast_v`. `slow_delay` waits once per slow row (at the first
  fast point), `fast_delay` waits at every point.
- **`multimegasweep`** — 2D grid where each axis is a **co-swept bundle**.
  `slow_params`/`slow_v_list` and `fast_params`/`fast_v_list` are parallel
  lists; per-axis all vectors must be equal length. The grid is
  `len(slow_v) × len(fast_v)`; at each grid point every slow param and every
  fast param is set together. Example — field-slow, (Vtg, Vbg)-line-fast:
  `s.multimegasweep([magnet.field], [B_vec], [k_tg.volt, k_bg.volt], [Vtgs, Vbgs], slow_delay=1, fast_delay=0.9)`.
- **`init_delay`** (2D only) — `True` applies `slow_delay` before the very
  first point; `False` skips it (the axis is already parked there).

All sweeps are SIGINT-interruptible: an interrupt finishes the current point,
sets `metadata['interrupted'] = True`, and marks the station interrupted (call
`reset()` or rebuild before the next sweep).

### `SweepResult` (dataclass)
`SweepResult(basedir, id, metadata, datapath)` — the run root, the integer run
id, the final `metadata` dict, and the on-disk `data.tsv.gz` path.

---

## Module-level helpers (`sweep.*`)

- `set_basedir(path)` — set the global `BASEDIR` used when a `Station` is built
  without an explicit `basedir`.
- `list_measurements(basedir=None)` — render a markdown table of runs in a
  basedir.
- `measurement_info(i, basedir=None)` — print one run's metadata.
- `set_shutdown_handler(fn)` / `request_shutdown()` — register a
  ramp-to-safe callback and trigger graceful shutdown (thread-safe; if a sweep
  is active it stops after the current point, then calls `fn`). Used by the UPS
  monitor.

---

## Data on disk (`sweep.db`)

Each run is a directory `<basedir>/<id>/` with `data.tsv(.gz)` (headerless TSV,
one row per point), `metadata.json`, and optional blobs (e.g. `plot.png`).

### `Writer(basedir, max_id=1_000_000, fsync_every=10)`
Creates the run directory at the lowest free integer id under `basedir`
(`.id`, `.dir`). `add_point(point)` / `add_points(points)` append rows
(fsynced every `fsync_every` points); `add_blob(name, bytes)` writes a sidecar
file (name may not be `data.tsv`/`data.tsv.gz`/`metadata.json`). `.metadata` is
a free dict saved to `metadata.json` on `close()`; on close the uncompressed
`data.tsv` is gzipped to `data.tsv.gz` (verified, then the plaintext removed).
Use as a context manager.

### `Reader(basedir, id)`
Reads a run back. `.metadata` (migrated to the current schema via
`migrate_metadata`), iteration yields rows of **strings** (no type conversion),
`all_data()` returns all rows, `blob(name)` reads a sidecar. `.datapath` is the
`data.tsv.gz` path. Use as a context manager. For numeric loads,
`np.loadtxt(reader.datapath, …)` or `hera.analysis.open_run`.

### Metadata keys written per sweep type
Common to all: `version`, `type` (`0D`/`1D`/`2D`), `function`, `columns`,
`comments`, `measurement_config`, `instruments`, `interrupted`, `start_time`,
`end_time`.

| function | additional keys |
|---|---|
| `sweep` | `param`, `setpoints`, `delay` |
| `multisweep` | `params`, `setpoints` (list of per-param vectors), `delay` |
| `megasweep` | `slow_param`, `fast_param`, `slow_setpoints`, `fast_setpoints`, `slow_delay`, `fast_delay` |
| `multimegasweep` | `slow_params`, `fast_params`, `slow_setpoints`, `fast_setpoints`, `slow_delay`, `fast_delay` |
| `watch` | `delay`, `max_duration` |

Two schemas coexist in older data — singular (`param`, `slow_param`) vs current
plural (`params`, `slow_params`). Read through `sweep.sweep_load` or
`hera.analysis.open_run`; don't hand-roll key access.

---

## Polygon rasters (`sweep.raster`)

Helpers for sweeping/plotting an arbitrary polygon region of a 2-D plane (e.g. a
bounded (Vtg, Vbg) window). A `multimegasweep` runs the rasterized point order;
these turn polygon vertices into that point list and back into a plot mesh.

### `rasterize(vertices, nx, ny, fast_axis, rev_x=False, rev_y=False)` → `(xs, ys)`
The x/y coordinates of the grid points **inside** the polygon. `vertices` is
`(N, 2)`; `nx`/`ny` are grid points per axis over the bounding box; `fast_axis`
is 0 if x is the inner (fast) axis, 1 if y; `rev_x`/`rev_y` reverse a sweep
direction. Returns two 1-D arrays in raster order — feed them as the co-swept
fast/slow vectors of a `multimegasweep`.

### `pcolorize_data(zs, vertices, nx, ny, fast_axis, rev_x=False, rev_y=False)` → `(xs_mat, ys_mat, zs_mat)`
Bin measured values `zs` (in rasterized point order) back onto the regular
bounding mesh for `plt.pcolormesh(xs_mat, ys_mat, zs_mat)`. Cells outside the
polygon are `NaN`. The `nx`/`ny`/`fast_axis`/`rev_*` arguments must match the
`rasterize` call that produced the sweep.

### `random_ngon_vertices(n)` → `(n, 2)` vertices
A random simple-ish n-gon, for tests/demos.

## Polygon rasters (`sweep.raster`)

Helpers for sweeping/plotting an arbitrary polygon region of a 2-D plane (e.g. a
bounded (Vtg, Vbg) window). A `multimegasweep` runs the rasterized point order;
these turn polygon vertices into that point list and back into a plot mesh.

### `rasterize(vertices, nx, ny, fast_axis, rev_x=False, rev_y=False)` → `(xs, ys)`
The x/y coordinates of the grid points **inside** the polygon. `vertices` is
`(N, 2)`; `nx`/`ny` are grid points per axis over the bounding box; `fast_axis`
is 0 if x is the inner (fast) axis, 1 if y; `rev_x`/`rev_y` reverse a sweep

fast/slow vectors of a `multimegasweep`.

But one density is not a call: the heavy partner was not resolved (25.8 T sits between the comb's 3rd and 4th members at 21.9 / 29.2 T), so the Luttinger sum is untested and a lone tone at 0.22·F_L is exactly what the investigation refuses to accept on a single column.

Per-column F(n) plus the partition sum f₁+f₂ = F_L is the read (investigation Steps 4–5). The window deliberately spans the **low-electron-density exception regime** (n ≲ 2×10¹², where ABAB legitimately mimics an ABCA singleton) into the discriminating region — the trajectory through it is the evidence, not any one column. n_max = +3.20×10¹² is the D = 0 line's TG-limited ceiling (V_tg = +0.9836, 16 mV under the limit; same point as run 6, so the fan's top column is directly comparable to the spot check).

assert_thermometry_live("T_sample", VTI.temp_logfile_candidates["T_sample"], max_age=15, max_period=12)
_T0, _B0 = T_sample(), magnet.field()
print(f"precondition T_sample = {_T0:.3f} K (1.0-1.5), B = {_B0:+.4f} T (|B|<0.05: magnet parked at 0), "
      f"V_si = {k_si():+.3f} V (0), nplci tg/bg = {k_tg.nplci()}/{k_bg.nplci()} (1/1), "
      f"PS heater {magnet.persistent_switch_on()}, output {magnet.output_enabled()}")
assert 1.0 <= _T0 <= 1.5 and abs(_B0) < 0.05 and abs(k_si()) < 0.01
assert k_tg.nplci() == 1 and k_bg.nplci() == 1
assert magnet.persistent_switch_on() and magnet.output_enabled()

# --- lock-ins: fixed for the whole fan. tau 0.3 -> 0.1 s so fast_delay = 1.0 s is a full 10 tau at 24 dB/oct. ---
print(f"lock-ins before: sr0 tau {sr0.time_constant()} s / {sr0.filter_slope()} dB, "
      f"sr1 tau {sr1.time_constant()} s / {sr1.filter_slope()} dB, sr1 sens {sr1.sensitivity()} V")
sr0.time_constant(TAU); sr1.time_constant(TAU)
sr1.sensitivity(50e-6)
assert sr0.time_constant() == TAU and sr1.time_constant() == TAU
print(f"lock-ins after:  tau {sr1.time_constant()} s, slope {sr1.filter_slope()} dB/oct -> fast_delay "
      f"{FAST_DELAY} s = {FAST_DELAY/TAU:.0f} tau; sr1 sens {sr1.sensitivity()} V "
      f"({sr1.sensitivity()/(sr1.amplitude()/1e8):.0f} Ohm FS); drive {sr1.amplitude()} V -> {sr1.amplitude()/1e8*1e9:.1f} nA")

# --- position the magnet at the fan's start (FastBi1K5 set blocks through the ramp; ~7.3 min from 0 T) ---
magnet.field(B_LO)
print(f"positioned: B = {magnet.field():+.4f} T (target {B_LO})")
assert abs(magnet.field() - B_LO) < 0.02

mc = dict(meas_config); mc["Si (V)"] = k_si(); mc["sample_temperature:"] = _T0
mc["comments"] = (f"landau-fan-vti electron D = 0: n {N_LO:+.2f} -> {N_HI:+.2f}e12 ({N_N} cols), "
                  f"B {B_LO} -> {B_HI} T ({len(B_vec)} rows, {DB*1e3:.0f} mT), tau {TAU} s, fast_delay {FAST_DELAY} s, sr1 50 uV")
s = sweep.AsyncStation(mc)
s.add_comment('landau-fan-vti')
s.add_comment(f'D = {D0} V/nm, n = {N_LO:+.2f} to {N_HI:+.2f}e12 cm^-2 ({N_N} pts, dn = {ns[1]-ns[0]:.4f}e12), '
              f'B = {B_LO} to {B_HI} T ({len(B_vec)} rows, dB = {DB*1e3:.0f} mT, d(1/B) = {_dinvB:.5f}/T, '
              f'F_Nyq = {0.5/_dinvB:.0f} T, dF = {1/(1/B_vec[0]-1/B_vec[-1]):.2f} T); electron side per sdh-spot-check run 6; '
              f'cal run 5: ratio {CAL["c_bg"]/CAL["c_tg"]:.3f}, n_offset {CAL["n_offset"]:+.3f}e12, D_offset {CAL["D_offset"]:+.3f}; '
              f'sr1 50 uV, tau {TAU} s / 24 dB, fast_delay {FAST_DELAY} s = 10 tau')
s.ramp(k_bg.volt, Vbgs[0]); s.ramp(k_tg.volt, Vtgs[0])
interruptible_sleep(10)

# row layout: [time, B, Vtg, Vbg, T_sample, k_tg.curr, k_bg.curr, sr0.X, sr0.P, sr1.X, sr1.P]
s.fp(T_sample).fp(k_tg.curr).fp(k_bg.curr)
s.fp(sr0.X).fp(sr0.P).fp(sr1.X).fp(sr1.P)
s.plot(k_tg.volt, sr1.X); s.plot(k_tg.volt, sr0.X)
s.plot('time', k_tg.curr); s.plot('time', k_bg.curr); s.plot('time', T_sample)

# Leak guard: trip on two CONSECUTIVE points over 1 nA. A single-point excursion at a row start is the
# gate-flyback charging transient (+-200 pA seen on run 5), not a sustained leak (session_notes TOOLING).
I_TRIP = 1e-9
_leak = {"n": 0}
def leak_guard(station, data):
    i_tg, i_bg = abs(float(data[5])), abs(float(data[6]))
    if i_tg > I_TRIP or i_bg > I_TRIP:
        _leak["n"] += 1
        print(f"leak excursion #{_leak['n']} at B={float(data[1]):+.3f} T, Vtg={float(data[2]):+.4f}: "
              f"|I_tg|={i_tg:.3e}, |I_bg|={i_bg:.3e} A")
        if _leak["n"] >= 2:
            print("LEAK TRIP (two consecutive points over 1 nA) — interrupting")
            station.interrupt_requested = True
    else:
        _leak["n"] = 0
s.register_run_after(leak_guard, ())

s.multimegasweep([magnet.field], [B_vec], [k_tg.volt, k_bg.volt], [Vtgs, Vbgs],
                 slow_delay=SLOW_DELAY, fast_delay=FAST_DELAY)
# endpoint by design: B = 6 T, gates at n = +3.20e12 — where the LK mass series wants them. No park, no re-traverse.
print(f"done: B = {magnet.field():+.3f} T, (Vtg, Vbg) = ({k_tg.volt():+.4f}, {k_bg.volt():+.4f}), "
      f"T_sample = {T_sample():.3f} K")
